parts.label: a
parts.technique: Spearman's rank correlation - dealing with tied ranks
parts.reason: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient is not mentioned anywhere in the 9MA0 statements; only PMCC is referenced (S5.1) and use of its formula is explicitly excluded. Rank correlation is a distinct topic not covered at all.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Calculating Spearman's rank correlation coefficient
parts.reason: No statement mentions rank correlation coefficients; only PMCC (S5.1) is referenced and explicitly its formula use is excluded. Spearman's coefficient is a different, uncovered concept.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Hypothesis test using Spearman's rank correlation critical values
parts.reason: S5.1 covers hypothesis testing extended to correlation coefficients but explicitly refers to PMCC (product moment correlation coefficient, denoted r/rho), not Spearman's rank correlation. This test uses Spearman's critical value tables, a different technique not covered.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Finding significance level from Spearman's critical value tables
parts.reason: Depends on Spearman's rank correlation coefficient framework, not covered by S5.1 which only refers to PMCC.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Unbiased estimates of population mean and variance from summary statistics
parts.reason: S2.3 covers calculating standard deviation from summary statistics, but the concept of an 'unbiased estimator' (dividing by n-1) for mean and variance of a population is not described in any statement; this is estimation theory not present in the spec.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Hypothesis test for difference of two population means using large-sample z-test
parts.reason: S5.3 only covers a hypothesis test for the mean of a single Normal distribution; there is no statement covering a two-sample test for difference of means. This is not in spec.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Justifying variance approximation from large samples
parts.reason: This part only makes sense as a follow-up justification for the two-sample test in (b), which is out of spec, and the underlying concept (large-sample approximation of variance) is not covered by any statement.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding sample mean from a confidence interval
parts.reason: Confidence intervals are not mentioned anywhere in the 9MA0 statements; this topic is entirely absent from the specification.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Deriving standard deviation from confidence interval width formula
parts.reason: Confidence interval theory and formulae are not covered by any statement in the specification.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Calculating confidence level from interval width using inverse normal
parts.reason: Confidence intervals are not part of the 9MA0 specification at all.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Sample size calculation for a required confidence interval width
parts.reason: Confidence interval theory, including sample size determination, is not mentioned in any statement.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Continuous uniform distribution model
parts.reason: The continuous uniform distribution is not mentioned in any statement; S3.1 only notes a general understanding that area under a curve represents probability for continuous distributions, without naming or requiring knowledge of the (continuous) uniform distribution as a model.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Mean and standard deviation of a continuous uniform distribution
parts.reason: Requires formulae for mean/variance of a continuous distribution, not covered by any statement (S4.2 explicitly excludes pdf-related derivations, and continuous uniform is not named anywhere).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Central Limit Theorem approximation for sample mean
parts.reason: S5.3 explicitly excludes 'Knowledge of the Central Limit Theorem or other large sample approximations'. This part directly requires the CLT.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Stating assumption for CLT application
parts.reason: Depends entirely on the CLT-based calculation in (c), which is explicitly excluded by S5.3.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Concept of a statistic vs parameter-dependent expression
parts.reason: This estimation-theory concept (distinguishing a statistic from an expression involving unknown parameters) is not covered by any statement in the specification.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Definition of unbiased estimator
parts.reason: Unbiased estimators (general estimation theory) are not mentioned anywhere in the statements; S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of mean/variance of discrete random variables, and no statement introduces the concept of an estimator.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Proving estimators are unbiased using E(aX+bY)
parts.reason: Requires expectation algebra for linear combinations of random variables, a concept (estimation theory) not present in any statement; general E(X) work is excluded (S4.1).

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Comparing variances of estimators for efficiency
parts.reason: Variance of linear combinations of random variables and estimator efficiency are not covered by any statement in the specification.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sum of independent normal random variables (linear combination) probability calculation
parts.reason: S4.2 covers a single Normal distribution and probabilities from it, but summing multiple independent normal variables to get a new normal distribution's parameters is not described in any statement.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Solving for number of people using sum of normals and quadratic inequality
parts.reason: Depends on the same sum-of-independent-normals technique as (a), which is not covered by any statement.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Chi-squared goodness of fit hypotheses
parts.reason: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit testing is not mentioned in any statement; S5.1-S5.3 only cover binomial proportion tests, correlation, and Normal mean tests.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.technique: Chi-squared test statistic and critical value comparison
parts.reason: Chi-squared distribution and goodness-of-fit test statistic are not covered anywhere in the specification statements.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.technique: Finding number of die rolls from chi-squared test result
parts.reason: Depends entirely on the chi-squared goodness-of-fit result from (b)(i), which is not covered by any statement.
